diagnostic.question: Can you explain the main purpose of arrays and iteration before reading?
diagnostic.answer: A complete answer should name the problem it solves, the values or control flow involved, and one mistake to avoid.

sections.title: Arrays store an ordered list
sections.body: An array uses zero-based integer indexes and has a length. It is appropriate when order and repeated items matter. Access outside the current range returns undefined. Arrays are objects, but Array.isArray distinguishes them from other objects.

sections.title: Some array methods change the array
sections.body: push, pop, shift, unshift, splice, sort, and reverse mutate the array. slice, concat, map, filter, and toSorted return a new array. In React, replacing state with a new array is easier to detect and reason about than mutating the existing state array.

sections.title: Iteration has a purpose
sections.body: for...of is clear for sequential work. forEach runs a callback for each item but returns undefined and cannot be stopped with break. map transforms every item into a new array, while find and filter answer different search questions. Start by naming the desired result.

sections.title: Empty and boundary cases
sections.body: An empty array is truthy, so check length when emptiness matters. The first element is at 0 and the last is at length - 1 or can be read with at(-1). Never assume an item exists after find or at an index; handle undefined explicitly.

sections.title: Why this matters in React
sections.body: Arrays and iteration is part of the JavaScript model React code already uses. Components, event handlers, state updates, list rendering, and data requests become easier to reason about when this concept is understood without framework shortcuts. Practise the JavaScript behavior first, then identify the same rule in JSX or a component.

interviewQuestions.question: Explain arrays and iteration to a junior developer.
interviewQuestions.answer: Use arrays for ordered collections. Recognize mutating and non-mutating operations. Choose iteration based on the result you need. Handle empty arrays and indexes.
interviewQuestions.followUp: Show a small example and one common mistake.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you prove that code using arrays and iteration behaves correctly?
interviewQuestions.answer: State the expected value or control flow first, test normal and boundary cases, and inspect the actual runtime result. Explain the JavaScript rule behind the evidence.
interviewQuestions.followUp: Which edge case would you test first?

interviewQuestions.question: Where can arrays and iteration affect React code?
interviewQuestions.answer: It can affect values, callbacks, rendering decisions, updates, or data flow. The exact connection depends on the concept; the important step is to reason from JavaScript behavior before blaming React.

commonMistakes.symptom: Code using arrays and iteration produces a surprising value.
commonMistakes.cause: The result was run before the value, type, scope, identity, or control flow was predicted.
commonMistakes.fix: Reduce the case, write the expected result, and apply the exact rule from the matching section.

commonMistakes.symptom: A learner copies syntax but cannot adapt it.
commonMistakes.cause: The example was memorized without explaining why it works.
commonMistakes.fix: Change the data and names, predict again, and explain which behavior must stay the same.

commonMistakes.symptom: A React problem is blamed on React immediately.
commonMistakes.cause: The underlying JavaScript behavior was not isolated first.
commonMistakes.fix: Reproduce the value or function behavior in a small JavaScript example, then reconnect it to the component.
